proof_summary: Let \(d=D(n)\), \(e=D(d)\), and \(q=(n-e)/9\); invariance of decimal digit sum modulo 9 makes \(q\) integral, and digit-sum bounds give \(d\le 10^q\) when \(q>0\). If \(q=0\), then \(d=e=n\) and \(10n\) is a partner; otherwise, pad the \(q\)-digit expansion of \(d-1\), adjoin its digitwise 9-complement to obtain a block of digit sum \(9q\) whose value is divisible by \(d\), and combine it (separated by zeros) with the digits of \(d\), producing a distinct \(k\) with \(D(k)=9q+e=n\) and \(d\mid k\).
